'''Donald George Fleming''' (born November 7, 1938) is a Canadian chemist. He attended the [[University of British Columbia]] and earned a [[Bachelor of Science]] degree in 1961 and a [[Master of Science]] degree in 1961. He earned a [[Ph.D.]] at the [[University of California, Berkeley]] in 1967. He is currently a professor emeritus of chemistry at the University of British Columbia.<ref>{{cite book|title=Directory of graduate research|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=lQj0AAAAMAAJ|year=1979|isbn=978-0-8412-0519-2}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|title=Reports of the President and of the Treasurer|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=_JLWAAAAMAAJ|year=1983|publisher=[[John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Foundation]]}}</ref> In 1989 he published a paper theorizing a new kind of [[chemical bond]], which he referred to as [[vibrational bond]]ing. The existence of such a short-lived bond was confirmed using a reaction between [[bromine]] and the [[exotic atom]] [[muonium]] in January 2015.<ref>[http://www.zmescience.com/science/chemistry/new-kind-chemical-vibrational-bond-0543543/ "A new type of chemical bond has been confirmed – the vibrational bond"]. ''ZME Science''. (January 29, 2015)</ref><ref>Amy Nordrum (January 20, 2015). [http://www.scientificamerican.com/article/chemists-confirm-the-existence-of-new-type-of-bond/ "Chemists Confirm the Existence of New Type of Bond"]. ''scientificamerican.com''.</ref> Fleming is also known for his work in utilizing muon beams in studies of physical chemical sciences.<ref>[https://www.chem.ubc.ca/prof-donald-fleming-named-aps-fellow-chemical-physics "Prof. Donald Fleming named an APS Fellow of Chemical Physics"]. ''ubc.ca''.</ref>
